stem.en: Which statement about the biological sex of a baby is correct?

text.en: The egg of the mother can carry either an X or a Y.

feedback.en: Females have XX, so every egg carries an X.

text.en: The food a mother eats in pregnancy decides the sex.

feedback.en: Food does not decide it. The chromosomes do, at fertilisation.

text.en: It is fixed by the hormones of the uterus in pregnancy.

feedback.en: It is fixed at fertilisation by the sex chromosomes.

text.en: It depends on whether the sperm has X or Y.

feedback.en: Correct. The mother gives an X, and the sperm gives an X or a Y by chance.

explanation.en: Females have XX and males have XY. Every egg carries an X, and a sperm carries an X or a Y. So the sex of a baby depends on which sperm fuses with the egg. This is chance, and it is never the mother's fault.

hints.en: Which parent can give a Y?
Does anyone choose which sperm reaches the egg?
